description: Mandeville, Louisiana: A City that Stays Afloat by Promoting Elevations is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by FEMA, Federal Emergency Management Agency. The City of Mandeville, located in St. Tammany Parish, decided to commit to helping residents escape troublesome flood waters. Finally tiring of the constant issue of a repeated damage-repair cycle, city officials decided to act by adopting high regulatory standards for the elevation of homes and businesses. Coverage: Louisiana (2023). The toolkit gives Louisiana as the location, 2023 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
